label: prop:algebraic-gns-embedding
title: Markov-trace GNS embedding $H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \hookrightarrow L(\mathcal{H})$ — operator-algebra route to the Archimedean side
html:
Let q > 0 be real, and give H_\infty(q) the *-structure fixed by \sigma_i^* = \sigma_i (extended conjugate-linearly and anti-multiplicatively). The QOU substrate q_0 \approx 1.11 is such a q. The infinite Hecke algebra H_\infty(q) := \varinjlim_n H_n(R, q) carries a unique tracial state \mathrm{tr}_M \colon H_\infty(q) \to R\otimes\mathbb{R} satisfying positivity \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* x) \geq 0. Write \mathcal{N} := \{x \in H_\infty(q) : \mathrm{tr}_M(x^* x) = 0\} for its trace ideal. The GNS construction yields a separable Hilbert space \mathcal{H} and a faithful *-representation of the trace-quotient

  \pi_{\mathrm{GNS}} \colon H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \;\hookrightarrow\;
    L(\mathcal{H}).

This realises the pre-Archimedean substrate as a concrete operator algebra.

Note (the quotient is not cosmetic). Under the canonical convention D the trace ideal is non-trivial: \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda with y_\lambda = 0 exactly when \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, so \mathcal{N} is the Temperley–Lieb radical and H_\infty(q)/\mathcal{N} \cong \mathrm{TL}_\infty(q). Faithfulness therefore holds on the quotient and not on H_\infty(q) itself. Under the excised convention C every y_\lambda was non-zero, \mathcal{N} collapsed to 0, and the two statements coincided.

Note (2026-10-10, the hypothesis). This statement previously assumed the "Wenzl positivity condition q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2} > 2" and placed q_0 just above it. For q > 0 that condition equals (q^{1/4} - q^{-1/4})^2 > 0, i.e. it only excludes q = 1, so it was never a threshold in q. Under convention D positivity holds for every real q > 0; see the proof.
